title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — Repair Coverage Determination
content:
## Coverage determination note

What a repair costs the building owner under the Preventive Maintenance Agreements depends on the tier's coverage switches on the repair coverage schedule. Where the tier covers repair labor, the labor on a covered unit is absorbed by the agreement; where it also covers parts, the parts are absorbed too; where the tier covers neither, the repair is billed in full at the tier's labor rate and list parts less the tier's repair labor and parts discounts. Compressor and heat exchanger replacement are absorbed only at a tier whose compressor and heat exchanger coverage switches are set, and at every other tier they are billed as non-covered work however well the rest of the unit is covered.

### Conditions on applying a repair to the allowance

1. **Status.** A repair is applied against the annual repair allowance only while the agreement stands in active status, read from the agreement record.
2. **No second decision.** A repair work order that already carries a coverage decision is not applied a second time; the work order number on the repair entries of the agreement's history decides whether a decision already stands.

### Refrigerant, the allowance and the deductible

Refrigerant is absorbed up to the tier's included pounds per term and billed at the published rate of 92 USD per pound beyond that. Where the absorbed value would carry the term past the tier's annual repair allowance, the allowance is exhausted first and the remainder is billed as non-covered work at the tier's discounted rates. Where the tier carries a deductible, that deductible is charged once per covered repair work order, whether or not the allowance absorbs the whole repair. The covered repair value absorbed in the term is the sum of the repair values applied to the allowance whose completion day falls between the term's first and last day inclusive.

**The owner's charge on a covered repair**, in words: the tier's deductible per covered repair, plus the part of the repair value that exceeds the allowance still remaining, plus the pounds of refrigerant used beyond the tier's included pounds multiplied by 92 USD per pound. A repair that is not covered at all is not priced this way; it is billed as non-covered work.

### Determinations (hypothetical)

- A covered repair valued at 3000 USD at a tier with 1000 USD of allowance remaining, a 250 USD deductible and no refrigerant used: the deductible of 250 USD is charged, the allowance absorbs 1000 USD, and 2000 USD is billed as non-covered work at the tier's discounted rates.
- A covered repair using 30 pounds of refrigerant at a tier with 25 pounds included and none yet used in the term: 5 pounds are billed at 92 USD per pound, that is 460 USD, in addition to any deductible.
- A compressor replacement at a tier whose compressor switch is off: billed as non-covered work, whatever the labor and parts switches say.
